record.narrative: This first round registers direct, falsifiable comparisons between molecular or technical exposures and each dependency score. For driver/gene-state hypotheses, the primary expectation is that cells carrying an activating alteration or loss in a related pathway will show a more negative dependency score (stronger dependency) in the matched or biologically connected outcome; these are registered with direction -1. For TP53 loss and MDM2 dependency, the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive because TP53 wild-type cells are often more MDM2 dependent, while TP53-loss cells may be less dependent. A technical crispr_library_avana comparison is included for a broadly essential process (POLR2A) to detect whether library-associated screen artifacts could confound later biological claims. Additional proposals cover less direct but plausible pathway links: MYC amplification with USP7/DHX9/KIF18A, EGFR amplification with TMED10, KRAS mutation with RIT1, and TP53 loss with RPL11. All proposals are initially unresolved and will be judged by effect size relative to the clinical-significance threshold, uncertainty intervals, and whether the direction matches the biological prediction. Independent validation will be reserved for findings with credible magnitude and direction.

Requesting the first twelve registered comparisons because they cover the strongest matched driver-loss hypotheses (KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR/ERBB2 amplifications with matched dependency, KEAP1 loss with NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with WRN dependency, TP53 loss with MDM2 dependency, MYC amplification with USP7/DHX9 dependency, and PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency), plus a technical screen-control using CRISPR library Avana for a broadly essential gene POLR2A. This selection maximizes early information about likely biological dependencies while checking whether library effects could inflate later claims. I deferred the more speculative pathway comparisons H13-H16 so the current evidence batch can be interpreted before allocating additional tests.

Estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction. Therefore, for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference below the comparator, i.e. stronger dependency; a negative signed estimate corresponds to the opposite raw direction. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds directly to a raw positive exposed-minus-comparator difference. The strongest new evidence supports three dataset-specific associations. H6 has signed estimate 0.784 with 95% interval 0.765 to 0.803, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly lower/more negative SMARCA2 dependency scores. H7 has signed estimate 0.790 with interval 0.760 to 0.819, meaning MSI-high cells have markedly lower WRN dependency scores. H11 has signed estimate 0.267 with interval 0.215 to 0.319, meaning PTEN-loss cells have lower STAT3 dependency scores. These effects are very large relative to the outcome scales and well beyond the 10% clinical-significance scale, so I accept H6, H7, and H11 within this dataset, while reserving mechanistic and generalizability claims. H5 is opposite to the registered direction: with direction -1, the signed estimate is -0.796, implying a raw positive difference of about +0.796. Thus KEAP1-loss cells have higher/less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores, so the original H5 claim is rejected and a reversed parent-linked claim is proposed. H3 is the most informative borderline claim: EGFR amplification is associated with a signed difference of about 0.025, near the 10% relative scale, but the interval barely includes zero. I leave H3 unresolved and request independent validation because validation is most useful for a clinically borderline claim. Most other direct comparisons are either tiny and opposite, or imprecise with intervals that cross zero. H2 and H10 are rejected because their intervals do not support a clinically meaningful effect in the expected direction. H1, H4, H8, and H9 are deferred: their point estimates are not compelling, but the intervals are broad enough that I do not want to overclaim rejection at this stage. H12 is a technical library control for a broadly essential process; it is imprecise and not followed further, though the large accepted biological effects remain subject to specificity checks. To assess possible global confounding behind H6, H7, H11, and reversed H5, I registered POLR2A negative-control comparisons for SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, and KEAP1 loss. POLR2A has relatively small variance and is expected to be broadly essential; large differences in POLR2A by these exposures would raise concern that the observed associations reflect broader cell-state or technical confounding rather than gene-specific dependency relationships.

The new validation evidence for H3 changes the assessment of the EGFR claim. H3 was registered with direction -1, so a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference below the comparator, meaning stronger EGFR dependency in EGFR-amplified cells. The discovery estimate for H3 was signed +0.025, which was near a roughly 10% relative effect scale but had a 95% interval that barely included zero. The independent validation estimate is signed only +0.006, with interval -0.034 to +0.045. Interpreted on the raw scale, validation therefore shows an EGFR-amplified minus non-amplified difference of about -0.006 EGFR dependency units, roughly 2% relative to the EGFR dependency mean, with uncertainty including null and clinically meaningful differences in both directions. The validation point estimate is far below the clinical-significance threshold and does not corroborate the borderline discovery result. Therefore the combined evidence does not support a reliable clinically meaningful association between EGFR amplification and stronger EGFR dependency in this dataset; H3 is rejected and closed.

I also reassess the reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 claim H17 using the same direct discovery evidence that caused the original H5 direction to be rejected. H17 is registered with direction +1, and its evidence is signed +0.796 with a very tight interval +0.776 to +0.816. On the raw scale, this means KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact cells, by a magnitude far above a 10% relative effect scale. This association is very large and precisely estimated within this dataset, so I accept H17 as a dataset-specific association while explicitly reserving mechanistic or generalizability claims. The original H5 claim remains rejected because the observed direction is opposite to the pre-specified stronger-dependency direction.

The previously accepted H6, H7, and H11 remain supported associations in this dataset: SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency; and PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. The technical POLR2A library control was not informative, and the next priority is specificity. If SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, or KEAP1 loss also produces large differences in the broadly essential POLR2A dependency score, that would suggest global screen or cell-state confounding and should lead to reassessment of these accepted associations. The most informative next analyses are therefore the reversed KEAP1-loss claim H17 already registered, the four POLR2A specificity controls H18-H21, and the still-untested direct pathway comparisons H13-H16. If the POLR2A controls are null, the accepted associations can remain strong dataset-specific findings; if any control is large, I will downgrade the corresponding accepted association as possibly non-specific. These conclusions are not causal and do not establish generalizability beyond the supplied dataset.

I am registering four targeted new comparisons to run alongside the eight already untested registered comparisons H13-H16 and H18-H21, so the next analysis batch can contain 12 informative tests. The accepted claims so far are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker/less-negative NFE2L2 dependency. The four new claims are designed to test nearby biology and context effects rather than repeat existing comparisons. First, arid1a_loss versus intact is a new direct predictor for dependency_SMARCA2. ARID1A and SMARCA4 are SWI/SNF complex components, so loss of another BAF component could produce a similar synthetic-lethal-like dependency on SMARCA2; registered direction -1 expects a more negative dependency score in arid1a-loss cells. Second, pik3ca_mutation versus wild type is a direct test for dependency_STAT3. Activating PIK3CA mutations can increase PI3K/AKT/STAT3 signaling, and PTEN loss already showed a positive association with stronger STAT3 dependency, so I anticipate a more negative STAT3 dependency score in PIK3CA-mutant cells; direction -1. Third, tp53_loss versus intact is a direct test for dependency_USP7. USP7 participates in MDM2-p53 regulation, and cells with TP53 loss are plausibly less dependent on USP7 through that axis, which would appear as a higher/less-negative dependency score in TP53-loss cells; direction +1. Fourth, EGFR dependency in KRAS wild-type versus KRAS mutant cells tests molecular context after EGFR amplification alone failed validation. If KRAS mutant cells bypass EGFR, they may be less EGFR-dependent, producing a more negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast for KRAS wild type and thus a positive signed estimate under direction -1. Alternative outcomes are null or opposite associations, which would argue against these mechanistic predictions and would be treated as evidence that the associations are not general across measured molecular contexts in this dataset. These claims are dataset-specific associations only; causality, therapeutic implication, and generalizability remain outside the immediate evidence.

Selecting twelve previously registered, currently untested comparisons: H13-H16, H18-H21, and H22-H25. These are the maximum informative batch because they cover untested direct pathway links, POLR2A specificity controls for the four accepted exposures, and nearby refinements of accepted SWI/SNF/PI3K/USP7/EGFR biology. The POLR2A controls are especially important: large differences for SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, or KEAP1 loss would raise concern that accepted effects reflect broader cell-state or screen artifacts rather than gene-specific dependencies. The nearby refinements test whether accepted pathways generalize across related molecular alterations or molecular contexts in the same dataset. No previously tested comparisons are repeated, so this batch adds new information.

The new batch mostly rejects the smaller pathway hypotheses and produces one very strong new association. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates mean weaker/higher dependency. H13-KRAS mutation with RIT1, H14-TP53 loss with RPL11, H15-MYC amplification with KIF18A, H16-EGFR amplification with TMED10, H22-ARID1A loss with SMARCA2, H23-PIK3CA mutation with STAT3, and H25-KRAS wild-type versus KRAS-mutant EGFR dependency all have point estimates near zero and intervals dominated by null; their upper bounds are at or below the roughly 10% clinical threshold. I reject these as unsupported dataset-specific associations and close them. H22 and H23 are important boundaries: the strong SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association does not extend to ARID1A loss, and the strong PTEN-loss/STAT3 association does not extend to PIK3CA mutation in this dataset. The POLR2A specificity controls H18-H21 are not informative positives: point estimates are tiny (about 0.4%-3% relative to POLR2A mean) and none approaches the enormous scale of accepted associations, although some intervals extend into the 10% region. This reduces, but does not eliminate, concern about global screen or cell-state confounding, so accepted H6, H7, H11, and H17 remain active dataset-specific associations. The major new result is H24: TP53 loss versus intact for dependency_USP7 has signed estimate +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467. Because H24 direction is +1, this is a raw positive difference: TP53-loss cells have markedly higher/less-negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, than TP53-intact cells. This is far above the 10% threshold and tightly bounded away from zero, so I accept H24 within this dataset. This is surprising because H8 TP53 loss with MDM2 was null, so I request independent validation of H24 before interpreting the mechanism. I also registered a POLR2A TP53-loss specificity control and a TP53-loss-by-KRAS-mutation interaction for USP7 to test whether H24 is non-specific or context-dependent. These conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

The independent validation for H24 strongly supports the TP53-loss/USP7 association. H24 has direction +1, so the reported signed estimates are raw exposed-minus-comparator differences on the dependency_USP7 scale. Discovery was +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467. Validation was +0.437 with independent interval +0.336 to +0.537. Because this is a direction +1 claim, a positive value means TP53-loss cells have higher, less-negative USP7 dependency scores than TP53-intact cells, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency. The magnitude is far larger than a roughly 10% relative effect threshold and remains bounded away from zero even under the stringent validation interval, so I accept H24 as a robust dataset-specific association. This does not establish causality or generalizability beyond the supplied dataset; it establishes that the association is stable within the supplied experimental system and validation split. I keep H24 active because context and specificity analyses remain useful. The prior POLR2A specificity controls for SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, and KEAP1 loss had very small point estimates relative to the large accepted associations, reducing concern about generic screen or cell-state confounding, but the TP53-loss POLR2A control H26 is still pending. The newly registered interactions ask whether accepted associations are stable across measured contexts: SMARCA4-loss effect by ARID1A loss for SMARCA2, PTEN-loss effect by PIK3CA mutation for STAT3, MSI-high effect by lineage subtype for WRN, and KEAP1-loss effect by STK11 loss for NFE2L2. The new USP7 cross-specificity proposals test whether SMARCA4 loss or PTEN loss also produce TP53-like USP7 effects. If those controls are large, I would downgrade the apparent specificity of the corresponding accepted associations; if they are near null, the accepted associations become more credible as dataset-specific, predictor-specific patterns. The next most informative analyses are therefore H26 and H27 plus these context/specificity proposals.

The currently registered untested set already contains the key pending specificity control for TP53 loss on the broadly essential POLR2A dependency and the context interaction for TP53 loss on USP7, plus cross-specificity and interaction checks for the accepted SMARCA2, WRN, STAT3, NFE2L2, and USP7 associations. I am adding two cross-specificity controls because the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 and MSI-high/WRN associations still have limited predictor-specific control evidence. First, SMARCA4 loss versus intact on dependency_NFE2L2, with direction +1, tests whether the huge KEAP1-loss-associated weakening of NFE2L2 dependency is predictor-specific or whether other common SWI/SNF-associated alterations also shift NFE2L2 dependency in the same or opposite direction. A near-null result would support the dataset-specific specificity of the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association; a large effect, in either signed direction, would weaken the inference that this is a predictor-specific relationship. Second, KEAP1 loss versus intact on dependency_WRN, with direction -1, tests whether the very strong MSI-high-associated strengthening of WRN dependency is specific to mismatch-repair-deficient biology or whether KEAP1-loss-associated cell state also alters WRN dependency. A near-null result supports WRN specificity; a large effect would suggest that accepted WRN associations may be less predictor-specific in this dataset. These are discovery-stage associations, not causal claims. The next analysis should consider H26 through H37 if possible, filling the 12-test slot with POLR2A controls, interactions, and reciprocal predictor-specificity checks.

I am requesting all twelve currently untested registered claims. This batch is the maximum informative set because it combines the still-pending TP53-loss POLR2A specificity control (H26), key context-interaction tests for accepted associations (H27-H31), direct USP7 cross-specificity checks for SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss (H32-H33), WRN/SMARCA2 cross-specificity checks (H34-H35), and the two new reciprocal specificity checks for NFE2L2/SMARCA4 loss and WRN/KEAP1 loss (H36-H37). These tests do not repeat previously analyzed comparisons, so they add new information without reusing old evidence. If POLR2A and cross-specificity controls are near null, the accepted associations remain credible as dataset-specific, predictor-specific patterns. If any control or interaction is large, the corresponding accepted association will be reinterpreted as less specific or context-dependent rather than globally homogeneous. These remain association analyses in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizability claims.

The new batch is dominated by well-behaved null and near-null control analyses, and it strengthens the internal credibility of the already accepted dataset-specific associations rather than adding new large effects. All estimates are already signed to the claim direction. H26 is the TP53-loss specificity control for POLR2A: signed estimate -0.014, 95% CI -0.034 to +0.006, n=406/1594. The point is about 5% of the POLR2A mean magnitude and is statistically compatible with zero; I reject it as an unsupported meaningful TP53-loss/POLR2A association and close it. This supports, though it does not prove, that the accepted TP53-loss/USP7 effect is not simply a global screen or essentiality shift. H27-H31 test context dependence. H27 USP7-by-KRAS interaction (+0.018, CI -0.152 to +0.188), H28 SMARCA2-by-ARID1A-loss interaction (+0.037, CI -0.015 to +0.089), H29 STAT3-by-PIK3CA interaction (+0.001, CI -0.150 to +0.152), H30 WRN-by-adenocarcinoma interaction (-0.021, CI -0.085 to +0.042), and H31 NFE2L2-by-STK11-loss interaction (-0.026, CI -0.079 to +0.026) all have point estimates below the roughly 10% clinical-scale criterion and include zero. I reject each as unsupported evidence for meaningful modification in this dataset, while noting that some subgroup intervals are wide and therefore do not establish precise absence of heterogeneity. H32-H37 are predictor-specificity controls. SMARCA4 loss or PTEN loss do not affect USP7 dependency (H32: -0.002; H33: -0.005). SMARCA4 loss does not affect WRN dependency (H34: +0.003), PTEN loss does not meaningfully affect SMARCA2 dependency (H35: +0.018, about 4% of the SMARCA2 mean), SMARCA4 loss does not affect NFE2L2 dependency (H36: -0.012), and KEAP1 loss does not affect WRN dependency (H37: +0.007). These controls are near null on the scale of the accepted effects, so they reduce concern that accepted associations reflect broad cell-state or technical confounding and increase the apparent predictor specificity of accepted H6, H7, H11, H17, and H24 within this dataset. I am requesting independent validation of H7 (MSI-high and dependency_WRN) because it is a large accepted effect in a relatively small MSI-high subgroup, and independent stability would make it a more reliable dataset-specific claim. No new causal or external-generalizability claim is made.

The newly delivered validation evidence strongly strengthens two accepted associations and definitively closes the remaining EGFR-amplification claim. All returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For H3 (direction -1, EGFR amplification versus no amplification on dependency_EGFR), validation is +0.0056 with independent interval -0.0338 to +0.0451. The point is very close to zero and much smaller than the roughly 10% relative threshold, and the interval includes zero. I reject H3 and close it: the supplied dataset does not support a meaningful EGFR-amplification association with EGFR dependency, and independent validation reinforces the null. For H7 (direction -1, MSI-high versus non-MSI-high on dependency_WRN), validation is +0.8218 with independent interval +0.7755 to +0.8681. Because the direction is -1, this signed positive effect corresponds to a raw lower, more-negative WRN dependency score in MSI-high cells, i.e. stronger WRN dependency. The magnitude is enormous relative to the dependency_WRN mean and far above the 10% clinical-scale threshold, with a very narrow independent interval. I accept H7 as a robust dataset-specific association and close the investigation, since the main effect is validated and context/specificity analyses were near null. This is not causal or external-generalizability evidence. For H11 (direction -1, PTEN loss versus intact on dependency_STAT3), validation is +0.3092 with independent interval +0.2322 to +0.3863. Signed positive means stronger, more-negative STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells. The effect is well above the 10% scale and bounded away from zero, so I accept H11 as a robust dataset-specific association and close the investigation. For H24, the previous independent validation (+0.4368, independent interval +0.3363 to +0.5374) already established a robust TP53-loss-associated weakening of USP7 dependency, and the subsequent context and specificity controls were small. I therefore keep H24 accepted but close further investigation. Current robust dataset-specific claims are H6, H7, H11, H17, and H24; H6 and H17 remain the most important unvalidated large accepted effects, with H6 the highest-priority next validation target if the next appraise stage permits a validation request. The evidence overall suggests several large, stable predictor-specific dependencies in this dataset, while many nearby pathway and technical/context controls remain near null or underpowered. I registered new context controls, especially CRISPR-library interactions for accepted effects and a culture-condition interaction for the MSI-high/WRN association, plus two additional WRN/NFE2L2 predictor tests. These are dataset-specific association analyses, not causal or generalizable claims.

The current untested set already contains important technical-context controls for the accepted effects: H38-H41 test whether the SMARCA4-loss, KEAP1-loss, PTEN-loss, and TP53-loss effects vary by Avana versus non-Avana CRISPR library; H42 tests culture-condition modification for the MSI-high/WRN effect; and H43-H44 test two new biological predictors, BRCA2 loss for WRN dependency and STK11 loss for NFE2L2 dependency. To use the next analysis slot for maximum additional specificity information, I am registering five cross-predictor/cross-outcome associations that directly probe whether the accepted associations are isolated predictor-specific signals or whether related predictors also alter the other major dependency outcomes. MSI-high versus MSI-stable is tested on dependency_DHX9, so a large signed effect would indicate that the MSI-high association is not limited to WRN in this dataset and may reflect a broader repair/cell-state association. SMARCA4 loss versus intact is tested on dependency_STAT3, which is also the outcome affected by PTEN loss; a large effect would weaken the inference that STAT3 dependency is uniquely associated with PTEN loss. KEAP1 loss versus intact is tested on dependency_SMARCA2, the outcome strongly affected by SMARCA4 loss; a large effect would suggest that KEAP1-loss cell state may shift SWI/SNF-associated dependency beyond NFE2L2. TP53 loss versus intact is tested on dependency_NFE2L2, because KEAP1 loss has the opposite-sign large effect on NFE2L2 and TP53 loss has a large USP7 effect; a large result would suggest overlap between accepted pathways rather than isolated predictor-specific effects. PTEN loss versus intact is tested on dependency_WRN, the outcome strongly affected by MSI-high; a large result would reduce the apparent specificity of both the PTEN-loss/STAT3 and MSI-high/WRN claims. All are dataset-specific association tests, not causal or generalizable claims. If these controls are near null relative to the 10% clinical-scale criterion, the accepted H6, H7, H11, H17, and H24 associations become more credible as predictor-specific patterns within the supplied data. If any is large, the corresponding accepted association should be reconsidered as less specific or as part of a broader measured-cell-state effect, and a subgroup-specific refinement may be needed. The next validation priority remains H6, then H17, if validation capacity is available after these discovery results.

I request all twelve currently untested registered claims, H38-H49. This uses the analysis slot to complete the highest-priority pending discovery work: technical-context interactions for the accepted large associations under the Avana versus non-Avana CRISPR library (H38-H41), culture-condition modification of the validated MSI-high/WRN effect (H42), two new predictor-specific hypotheses (H43-H44), and reciprocal cross-specificity tests designed to check whether accepted effects remain outcome/predictor-specific or instead reflect broader cell-state patterns (H45-H49). If estimates and intervals remain far from the roughly 10% relative clinical-scale criterion, these analyses strengthen specificity and contextual stability within the supplied dataset. If any comparison shows a large effect or a broad interval compatible with a clinically meaningful effect, the corresponding accepted claim will be reassessed, deferred, or refined. No assessments are returned now because no new results have yet been analyzed.

All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed value supports the claimed direction. H38-H49 were mostly technical-context or predictor-specificity controls. H38 (SMARCA2/SMARCA4 by Avana, signed -0.0198, 95% CI -0.0762 to +0.0365), H39 (NFE2L2/KEAP1 by Avana, +0.0022, -0.0506 to +0.0550), and H41 (USP7/TP53 by Avana, +0.0837, -0.1632 to +0.3306) do not provide reliable evidence for meaningful modification of the accepted SMARCA4, KEAP1, or TP53 main effects. The H41 point is not negligible, but the interval is extremely wide and includes zero; the non-Avana TP53-loss cell is small. I reject these as unsupported context effects. H43-H49 are new predictors or cross-specificity checks; all point estimates are small or statistically compatible with zero: BRCA2 loss on WRN, STK11 loss on NFE2L2, MSI-high on DHX9, SMARCA4 loss on STAT3, KEAP1 loss on SMARCA2, TP53 loss on NFE2L2, and PTEN loss on WRN. I reject these as unsupported associations, while noting that confidence intervals are not formal equivalence bounds. The two exceptions are H40 and H42. H40 (PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 modified by Avana library) has signed estimate +0.1958, 95% CI +0.0333 to +0.3584; the point is about 70% of the validated PTEN-loss main effect on STAT3, but the non-Avana PTEN-loss cell has only 27 exposed samples, so I keep it unresolved and active rather than accepting an unadjusted, possibly unstable context claim. H42 (MSI-high effect on WRN modified by adherent culture) has signed estimate +0.1046, 95% CI +0.0370 to +0.1722. The lower bound is just above the approximate 10% outcome-mean scale for dependency_WRN, but the comparison involves a small non-adherent MSI-high cell and multiple unadjusted tests. I keep H42 unresolved and active and request independent validation of H42; validation will decide whether the culture-dependent difference is stable enough to refine the robust H7 claim. The original main effects H7 and H11 remain accepted as overall dataset-specific associations, but I keep their investigations active because these context interactions may be important refinements.

All estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For H24 (TP53 loss versus intact, direction +1, dependency_USP7), discovery was +0.396 (95% CI +0.325 to +0.467) and independent validation was +0.437 (independent interval +0.336 to +0.537). This is a very large effect on the dependency_USP7 scale and is bounded away from zero after independent validation. I therefore accept H24 as a robust dataset-specific association and close it: TP53 loss is associated with weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency in this dataset. This is not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H42 (adherent-culture modification of the MSI-high/WRN effect, direction -1), discovery gave +0.105 (95% CI +0.037 to +0.172), but independent validation gave -0.011 (independent interval -0.121 to +0.099). The validation point is essentially null and opposite in sign, and the independent interval does not support a stable positive adherent-culture interaction. I reject H42 as a supported context-specific refinement, while noting that its validation interval is not an equivalence proof against every possible small or opposite interaction. This rejection does not undermine the overall MSI-high/WRN claim: H7 remains robustly accepted with discovery +0.790 (95% CI +0.760 to +0.819) and independent validation +0.822 (independent interval +0.776 to +0.868). Given the validated main effect and the failed culture interaction, I close H7. I also close the main H11 association because PTEN-loss/STAT3 was validated (+0.309, independent interval +0.232 to +0.386). However, H40 remains active because its discovery library interaction is still potentially important; the registered simple-effect analyses in Avana and non-Avana library contexts (H51 and H52) are the appropriate next refinement. Current robust dataset-specific associations are H6, H7, H11, H17, and H24, with H6 and H17 now the highest-priority unvalidated accepted effects. The next best analyses are H50-H52: check whether WRN/MSI-high remains strong within adherent culture, and decompose the PTEN-loss/STAT3 library-context signal. After those, validation should target H6 first, then H17. These conclusions describe associations in the supplied data, not causality or generalizable biology.

No evidence is due for assessment at this explore stage. I register nine new, untested comparisons to complement the three active refinements H50-H52 and fill the next analysis slot. First, three predictor-specific biological hypotheses test additional measured binary predictors: MYC amplification may strengthen dependency_POLR2A because MYC-amplified cells can be transcription-addicted; RB1 loss may strengthen dependency_WRN through replication-stress biology; NF1 loss may alter dependency_STAT3 through RAS/MAPK and inflammatory-signal rewiring. These are dataset-specific association tests, not causal claims. Second, three high-frequency research-marker main associations test markers D, E, and F as latent measured predictors. Because these markers have no assigned gene or pathway, any large association would be interpreted as a dataset-specific pattern, possibly a useful subgroup assay or potential confounder, rather than as generalizable biology. Third, three lineage-subtype interaction refinements test whether the currently accepted large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, and PTEN-loss/STAT3 associations are uniform across adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma lung subtype or instead concentrated in the dominant adenocarcinoma stratum. A large positive signed interaction would support a subtype-specific refinement; a small or zero interaction would support treating the parent effects as broader within this dataset. The active H50-H52 remain important for decomposing WRN/MSI-high adherent-cell behavior and PTEN-loss/STAT3 library context. Validation priority remains H6 then H17 after the next discovery results arrive.

No assessments are due because no new discovery results are currently awaiting appraisal. I request the twelve highest-priority untested registered claims: H50-H52 decompose the currently active context questions for WRN/MSI-high and STAT3/PTEN-loss; H53-H55 add biologically motivated predictor-specific tests for MYC amplification on POLR2A, RB1 loss on WRN, and NF1 loss on STAT3; H56-H58 screen high-frequency constructed research markers as possible latent predictors of SMARCA2, WRN, and STAT3 dependency; and H59-H61 test whether the three accepted or partially validated large effects vary by lineage subtype. All estimates will already be signed to the registered claim direction. After these results arrive, I will use the 10% relative clinical-significance scale, interval bounds, cell sizes, and multiplicity to decide whether to accept, reject, defer, or refine each claim, and then prioritize independent validation for the most consequential currently unvalidated accepted effects, especially H6 and H17.

All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claim and negative values oppose it. Using an approximate absolute 10% outcome-mean scale for clinical significance, H50 (MSI-high effect on dependency_WRN within adherent culture) has a very large signed estimate of +0.813 with 95% CI +0.780 to +0.846, far above the relevant WRN threshold and with adequate cells; I accept it as a dataset-specific refinement supporting the robust overall MSI-high/WRN association. H51 (PTEN-loss effect on dependency_STAT3 within Avana library) has estimate +0.288, CI +0.232 to +0.343, also robustly clinically meaningful and consistent with the validated main PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect; I accept and close it.
